messages:
maria.gomez: Quick sync — I want to align on the operator-token broker migration and what telemetry/audit we must add before we flip. TL;DR: move from long-lived project API keys to short-lived operator-issued tokens for infra services. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 on short-lived tokens. main asks: how do we map scopes (project vs org) and what does the broker API look like?
lisa: We should also define rollout strategy: start with a small set of non-customer-facing infra services to validate rotations and KMS integration.
zach: Telemetry must include token issuer id, original requestor (if impersonated), scope, TTL, and minting reason. That helps investigations.
samir: Edge: third-party webhooks that only support static headers. How do we handle them? Maybe a proxy that mints a long-lived credential and stores it in a vault.
maria.gomez: Good call on telemetry. Proposed minimal broker response: ```json
{
  "token": "<jwt>",
  "expires_at": "2024-12-01T15:04:05Z",
  "scopes": ["project:read:myproj"],
  "issued_by": "operator-broker-v2",
  "origin": "service-A"
}
```
We log token_id, issued_by, origin, scopes, and reason. No plaintext token in audit logs.
kevin: For scope mapping: allow requested scope alias (e.g., svc-role=datastore-reader) that broker verifies against service identity and policy. Broker should reject privilege escalation.
lisa: Migration plan idea: 1) introduce broker behind feature flag, 2) instrument 10 services to request ephemeral tokens, 3) enable rotation for 30 days, 4) cutover for other infra. Canary on a on-call pager before wide rollout.
zach: Also add metrics: mint_latency, mint_fail_rate, active_token_count, tokens_by_scope. Dashboards + alerts for mint_fail_rate > 1% over 5m.
samir: For webhooks we can support an outbound-proxy component that mints short-lived tokens and caches a long-lived vault secret only for the proxy. That keeps overall posture while supporting legacy endpoints.
maria.gomez: Security nit: broker must do key wrapping with our KMS and support key rotation without invalidating active tokens (i.e., verify with signed keyset). Consider JWK rotation semantics.
kevin: Agreement. Add a revocation path: central revocation list + short TTL so revocation window small. We cannot rely solely on revocation if TTLs are long.
lisa: Ops question: who gets alert for unusual mint volume by a service? Suggest playbook: if a service mints > 5x baseline, auto-create incident for Sec/Platform triage.
zach: Implementation sketch for mint endpoint: ```
POST /v2/mint
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <svc-assertion>
Body: {"requested_scopes": ["project:write:foo"], "ttl_s": 3600, "reason": "ci-runner"}
```
Return short-lived JWT signed with broker key and token_id.
kevin: We must also support impersonation: operator can mint on behalf of user with an explicit audited header. Broker validates impersonation rights.
maria.gomez: Ok next steps: 1) draft API contract and JWK rotation behavior (kevin), 2) telemetry/metrics shape (zach), 3) migration canary checklist (lisa), 4) webhook-proxy design (samir). I'll open RFC follow-up and assign.
auth-bot: Created RFC-3812 in repo: /rfc/operator-token-broker-migration, link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/3812 :sparkles:
maria.gomez: Thanks — will post the checklist in #eng-ops once RFC is up. :thumbsup:
